Marissa — reviewed the attachments. Summary and recommended asks below (feel free to paste into an email to FinHealth):

Summary of what we saw: SOC2 Type II (2026-03) looks standard; pen test exec summary shows a mix of low/medium findings and a couple of medium-high items (no confirmed criticals in the summary). Vendor: SecureCheck Labs — reputable.

Recommended vendor acceptance & required items:
- Request: redacted full pen test report (remove customer-identifying data) signed NDA if FinHealth prefers.
- Vulnerability management SLAs (we recommend we ask them to commit in writing):
  - P1 (critical, CVSS 9.0-10): initial acknowledgement within 4 hours, mitigation/patch ETA within 72 hours or documented compensating controls; 7-day remediation commit where feasible.
  - P2 (high, CVSS 7.0-8.9): acknowledgement within 24 hours, remediation within 14 days.
  - P3/P4 (medium/low): monthly triage, remediation within 30-90 days depending on risk.
- Scanning cadence: internal + third-party pen test annually; authenticated scans/DAST quarterly for externally facing services; SCA/secret scanning weekly where applicable.
- Disclosure policy: require 90-day remediation window before any public disclosure; coordinate through a named security contact.
- CVSS threshold for automatic escalation to us: >=7.0.

Operational asks:
- Provide a named security contact + their PGP/secure intake channel (email + phone).
- Confirm whether they accept coordinated disclosure and the 90-day window.
- Share their remediation tracking (Jira or equivalent) for any high/critical items we assess as in-scope.

I'll draft a short template email we can send to Alex/Jenny with these asks. Thoughts?

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
